content: CCL16, also known as Chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 16, is a small cytokine that belongs to the CC chemokine family. It is also referred to by other names, including Liver-expressed chemokine (LEC) and Monotactin-1 (MTN-1). This chemokine is primarily expressed in the liver, thymus, and spleen. It exhibits chemoattractive properties, specifically targeting monocytes and lymphocytes. The expression of CCL16 in monocytes can be significantly upregulated by the presence of interleukin-10 (IL-10), interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), and bacterial lipopolysaccharides. The gene encoding CCL16 is located on chromosome 17 in humans, within a cluster of other CC chemokine genes. CCL16 exerts its biological effects by interacting with specific cell surface chemokine receptors, including CCR1, CCR2, CCR5, and CCR8. Elevated levels of CCL16 have been detected in human blood plasma. This chemokine may play a role in the trafficking of eosinophils, as it has been found to exhibit functional affinity for H4 receptors, which are expressed on eosinophils and mast cells. Additionally, CCL16 has been shown to suppress the rapid proliferation of myeloid progenitor cells, indicating a potential regulatory role in hematopoiesis.
